recent_posts.title: PCPJack worm targets systems already compromised by TeamPCP, steals credentials and spreads across cloud infrastructure
recent_posts.summary: SentinelOne researchers have discovered PCPJack, a Linux worm that uniquely targets systems already infected by the cybercrime group TeamPCP. Rather than scanning for fresh victims, PCPJack evicts TeamPCP's malware and takes over the compromised infrastructure. It then spreads across cloud environments by scanning for exposed Docker, Kubernetes, Redis, MongoDB, and RayML services, harvests SSH keys for lateral movement, and exfiltrates encrypted credentials via Telegram. The group also exploits known CVEs including a Next.js authentication bypass and WordPress plugin vulnerabilities. The identity of the PCPJack operators remains unknown. Recommended mitigations include enforcing MFA, switching to IMDSv2 on AWS, and avoiding plaintext secret storage.

recent_posts.title: Apple is talking to Intel and Samsung about making its M-series chips
recent_posts.summary: Apple is in early-stage exploratory talks with Intel and Samsung about manufacturing some of its M-series chips, aiming to reduce total dependence on TSMC as its sole 3nm chip supplier. No orders have been placed. The most likely scenario would keep high-performance chips on TSMC while shifting lower-end M-series to an alternative foundry, with non-TSMC shipments unlikely before mid-2027. The primary obstacle is yield consistency — both Intel Foundry and Samsung have historically struggled to match TSMC's manufacturing quality. Intel's stock surged to an all-time high on the news, buoyed by recent restructuring under CEO Lip-Bu Tan, a US government stake, and new customers like Amazon and Terafab. However, Intel's foundry business still holds under 5% market share and lost $2.4 billion in Q1 2026. Apple's motivation is supply chain resilience and negotiating leverage with TSMC, not cost reduction.

recent_posts.title: PHP retires its custom license in favor of BSD three-clause
recent_posts.summary: The PHP project has officially retired its custom PHP License and relicensed its codebase under the three-clause BSD license. The old PHP License 3.01 and Zend Engine License 2.0 were problematic: neither was OSI-approved, both were GPL-incompatible, and they caused recurring headaches for Linux distribution packagers. Ben Ramsey led the effort starting July 2025, tracking down original PHP Group members for written consent and securing sign-off from Perforce Software (owner of Zend Engine rights). The RFC also proposes removing build-time linking options for GPLv3 libraries (GNU Readline and GDBM) to further simplify packaging. The vote passed 47–0 with 2 abstentions.

recent_posts.title: Google's Fitbit Air is a $100 screenless band with a Gemini AI health coach
recent_posts.summary: Google has announced the Fitbit Air, a $100 screenless fitness tracker launching May 26. Weighing 12 grams, it tracks heart rate, SpO2, HRV, sleep, and AFib with up to one week of battery life. The device pairs with a $10/month Google Health subscription that includes a Gemini-powered AI coach for personalized workout plans and meal photo nutrition analysis. The Fitbit app is being rebranded as the Google Health app, available on both iOS and Android. Existing Fitbit users face a forced account migration to Google accounts by May 19, with data deletion starting July 15 for non-migrators — raising GDPR concerns in Europe.

recent_posts.title: MuddyWater uses Chaos ransomware as cover for espionage operations
recent_posts.summary: Iranian state-sponsored group MuddyWater is using Chaos ransomware as a cover for espionage operations. Attacks begin with Microsoft Teams-based social engineering to harvest credentials and manipulate MFA, followed by deployment of remote management tools (AnyDesk, DWAgent) and a custom backdoor disguised as a Microsoft WebView2 app. The ransomware messaging — including extortion emails and leak site postings — is largely theater designed to distract incident responders while credential theft and data exfiltration occur in parallel. Rapid7 attributes the campaign to MuddyWater with moderate confidence based on overlapping C2 infrastructure and code-signing certificates. The tactic mirrors approaches used by China-linked ChamelGang and North Korean actors, representing a growing pattern of state-sponsored groups borrowing financially motivated cybercrime aesthetics to obscure their true objectives.

recent_posts.title: Former Gearbox Quebec founders launch Ricochet Games, a small self-funded studio focused on co-op action-adventure
recent_posts.summary: Several veterans from Gearbox Studio Québec, including former co-studio heads Sébastien Caisse and Pierre-André Déry and ex-Borderlands creative director Maxime Babin, have founded Ricochet Games, a self-funded independent studio in Québec, Canada. The team, which also brings experience from Call of Duty and Assassin's Creed, is deliberately keeping the studio small to avoid the boom-bust cycle seen at other veteran-led studios. Their first project is a buy-to-play co-op action-adventure game for PC and console, with studio inspirations including Arrowhead and Remedy, and creative references from Studio Ghibli and FromSoftware. The launch follows Take-Two's 2024 acquisition of Gearbox, which led to layoffs at both companies.

recent_posts.title: Valve to restock Steam Controller after selling out in under an hour
recent_posts.summary: Valve's newly relaunched Steam Controller sold out in under an hour, with the company promising a restock timeline soon. Scalpers are already listing the $100 device on eBay for up to $400. In other gaming industry news, Supercell is acquiring Metacore, the Finnish studio behind Merge Mansion, a mobile game with over 60 million downloads and $700 million in revenue since 2020.

recent_posts.title: Windsurf adds Devin Review and Quick Review for AI-powered code review in the IDE
recent_posts.summary: Windsurf 2.0 introduces two AI-powered code review tools. Devin Review reorganizes PR diffs by logic rather than file order, groups related edits, flags bugs with explanations, and supports an Autofix workflow where Devin generates and applies fixes directly. Quick Review is a faster, locally-run option powered by SWE-check, a bug detection model claimed to be up to 10x faster than a full deep-review agent, designed for catching bugs before opening a PR.

recent_posts.title: AI data centre demand is crushing consumer memory supply, and prices are spiking across the board
recent_posts.summary: AI data centres are consuming DRAM at a pace that fabs cannot match, triggering a severe shortage in consumer electronics. Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron have shifted production toward high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI servers, which requires three times the wafer capacity of standard DDR5. DRAM contract prices surged 90% in Q1 2026, DDR5 retail prices are six to eight times higher than September 2025 levels, and hyperscaler capex is on track to exceed $650 billion in 2026. The downstream effects are already visible: Apple raised Mac Mini prices, Sony raised PS5 prices by $100, Nintendo is absorbing 40% higher RAM costs for Switch 2, and Valve delayed its Steam Machine. IDC projects 10-20% price increases across consumer electronics and an 11.3% PC market contraction. New fab capacity takes two to three years to come online, and multi-year supply agreements between chipmakers and major tech companies suggest no near-term relief.

recent_posts.title: Unity AI open beta: what it does, what it costs, and where it falls short
recent_posts.summary: Unity has launched Unity AI as an open beta integrated into the Unity 6 editor, replacing the deprecated Unity Muse suite. It offers three modes: Ask (Q&A), Plan (structured implementation planning), and Agent (direct project changes via natural language). Agent mode supports scene manipulation, script generation, polygon auditing, lighting matching, and 3D asset creation from images, with checkpoint-based rollback and tagged AI assets. Generative tools cover 3D meshes (via Tripo and Hana 3D), animation, voice synthesis (ElevenLabs), sound effects, materials, and 2D assets — intended as prototyping placeholders. An AI Gateway and MCP server allow connecting external models like Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and Cursor. Pro/Enterprise/Industry subscribers get 2,000 credits/month included; Personal Edition users get a 14-day trial then $10/month. Community reception is mixed: the agentic assistant gets positive marks for scene work, while 3D mesh quality and copyright concerns around generative assets remain unresolved.
